rationale: The answer gets the central facts right. It identifies the two 2026 Reg. 26(2) exceptions: different cut-offs for cash versus in-kind dealing, and for hedged versus unhedged classes. It also correctly separates these from the older Q&A 1030 reasoned-waiver route, and warns against reading the exceptions as a general permission for any class-level cut-off variation. However, it has substantive weaknesses. (1) It says only 'currency-hedged versus unhedged classes' and omits the key qualifier that the hedging must be at class level. The grader notes stress that the exception does not cover every kind of hedged class. (2) It adds conditions not found in the key points ('where the operational differences justify them and the arrangements are properly disclosed'). This risks importing a justification-style requirement into the express exceptions, which the grader notes warn against. (3) It does not state that dealing procedures and frequencies otherwise remain the same. It also calls the 2026 instrument 'guidance' rather than regulations, a minor inaccuracy. The central content is useful but has a material omission and an added qualification, so partial.
